commits.message:
Reference test no longer includes user's .vimrc; adjusted script to set
some vimrc settings that tests were depending upon; adjusted one test to
not depend on a setting that it didn't make sense to depend on.
Added test for backspace in insert mode affecting yank buffer

Added more tests

Filled out the rest of the level 3 motion tests. Added tests for
backspace in insert mode and its interaction with repetition and undo
history.

Better test runner, fixed level 3 tests

The previous version of the vimscript testrunner would parse files, and
try to run tests as it got to them. This didn't work very well, because
the best way to simulate keyboard input - feedkeys() - doesn't simulate
the keys immediately, but rather puts them in a queue, and simulates
them after returning all the way out. The old testrunner used :normal
instead of feedkeys, which sort-of worked but messed up the undo
history, and then the workaround for the undo history caused problems
with marks.  This commit mostly rewrites the testrunner to use feedkeys;
it first parses all the files, then each test calls feedkeys for the
keystrokes required to run it, followed by \<esc>:RunNextTest()\n.
Added level 3 unit tests (slightly broken) and some testrunner changes
Finished level 2 tests, testrunner handles undo history

Partial vim testcase handler

The goal of this is to have a set of "vim unit tests" which non-vim text
editors that're adopting vim keybindings can adopt easily. The regular
vim unit tests aren't suitable for this, because (a) they're heavy on
complex vimscript, which a non-vim editor probably won't have, and (b)
they're too hard. So we have an easy-to-parse test case format, and a
vimscript program that'll execute them against real-vim as a reference
solution.

This commit starts the repository, adds half of the reference tester,
and provides a single example test case to demonstrate the syntax.
